neighbours.label: the verb or preposition right after a distributive 'each X' subject ('Each chapter covers', 'each one in lieu of')
fire: The book has twelve parts, and each chapter deals with a different decade.
In this course, each lesson focuses on a single grammar point.
The teacher gave out cards, and each card showed the name of a planet.
There are five rooms upstairs, and each room faces the garden.
The museum has four halls, and each hall covers one period of history.
We planted ten trees, with each tree in memory of a former pupil.
The report has six sections, and each section ends with a summary.
The players got new shirts, and each shirt carries the number of its owner.
quiet: The book has twelve parts, and the last chapter deals with a different decade.
In this course, the first lesson focuses on a single grammar point.
The teacher gave out cards, and the big card showed the name of a planet.
There are five rooms upstairs, and the main room faces the garden.
The museum has four halls, and the new hall covers one period of history.
We planted ten trees, with one old tree in memory of a former pupil.
The report has six sections, and the final section ends with a summary.
The players got new shirts, and the captain's shirt carries a gold number.
